metadata.title: aichat GPT-5.5 Tool Calling Bug - Knowledge Graph
metadata.description: Knowledge graph of findings from investigation into aichat's OpenAI GPT-5.5 'Invalid Responses API response data' error
metadata.method: manual construction from 14 research findings (graphify semantic extraction unavailable due to expired AWS SSO)

nodes.label: Observed Error
nodes.description: Error: Failed to call chat-completions api / Caused by: Invalid Responses API response data

nodes.label: Empty Output Array
nodes.description: GPT-5.5 returns output:[] with status:'completed', 0 output tokens, 0 reasoning tokens

nodes.label: bail!() at bedrock.rs:982
nodes.description: Response parser crashes with bail! when output is empty instead of handling gracefully

nodes.label: Graceful Handler in openai.rs:427
nodes.description: Chat Completions handler returns empty with warn!() - the correct pattern

nodes.label: Strict Mode Auto-Normalization
nodes.description: Responses API auto-normalizes schemas to strict mode when 'strict' field is omitted, adding all properties to required and setting additionalProperties:false

nodes.label: Missing strict:false in aichat
nodes.description: aichat never sets 'strict' field on tool schemas (0 occurrences in src/). Without explicit strict:false, Responses API auto-normalizes to strict

nodes.label: Schema Strict Mode Violations
nodes.description: 12/22 tools have properties not in required array (48 total violations). ALL 22 tools missing additionalProperties:false

nodes.label: GPT-5.5 Literal Compliance Behavior
nodes.description: GPT-5.5 'interprets prompts in a literal and thorough manner' - refuses rather than violates schema constraints

nodes.label: 22 Tools Exceed Soft Limit
nodes.description: 22 tools exceed OpenAI's recommended <20 per turn. More tools = more constraint conflicts

nodes.label: JsonSchema Struct Limitation
nodes.description: JsonSchema struct at function.rs:127-149 has no additionalProperties field - structurally cannot represent strict-mode compliance

nodes.label: Zero-Transformation Schema Pipeline
nodes.description: Schema pipeline is pure passthrough: functions.json → deserialize → filter → serialize. No validation or strict-mode compliance checking

nodes.label: Unreviewed Custom Patch (b92c83d)
nodes.description: Responses API code in bedrock.rs is a local custom patch (Jun 3, 2026). PR #1318 was rejected upstream. No code review caught the bail!() or missing strict:false

nodes.label: OpenAI Responses API
nodes.description: Newer API that replaces Chat Completions. Different default behavior: auto-normalizes to strict mode vs Chat Completions' non-strict default

nodes.label: OpenAI Chat Completions API
nodes.description: Legacy API. Non-strict by default - schemas work as best-effort matching without normalization

nodes.label: bedrock.rs (Responses API Client)
nodes.description: Custom implementation handling Bedrock OpenAI models via Responses API. Contains build_responses_api_body (818-928) and response parsers (932-992)

nodes.label: openai.rs (Chat Completions Client)
nodes.description: Standard Chat Completions implementation with graceful empty-output handling

nodes.label: function.rs (Schema Definitions)
nodes.description: Contains JsonSchema struct, FunctionDeclaration, and Functions::init() for loading tool schemas

nodes.label: gui_session Tool (Worst Offender)
nodes.description: 13/14 properties missing from required array - most severely violated tool schema

nodes.label: ralph_loop Tool (Mutually Exclusive Params)
nodes.description: 10/10 properties missing from required - contains mutually exclusive parameters that cannot all be satisfied simultaneously

nodes.label: Single Tool Call Works Fine
nodes.description: User observation: '1 simple tool call works just fine' - consistent with root cause since single compliant tool has no constraint conflicts

nodes.label: PR #1318 (Responses API) Rejected
nodes.description: Upstream maintainer explicitly rejected Responses API support (Jun 2025). Code appeared anyway in bedrock.rs as custom patch

nodes.label: PR #1340 (Empty Output Fix - Chat Completions Only)
nodes.description: Fixed empty output handling only for openai.rs, NOT for bedrock.rs Responses API handler

nodes.label: Fix: Add strict:false to bedrock.rs
nodes.description: One-line fix: add '"strict": false' to tool schema JSON in bedrock.rs:913-924. Opts out of auto-normalization

nodes.label: Fix: Graceful Empty Output Handling
nodes.description: Replace bail!() with warn!() + return empty at bedrock.rs:981-982, matching openai.rs pattern

nodes.label: Fix: Make Schemas Strict-Compliant
nodes.description: Add additionalProperties:false to JsonSchema, put all props in required, use nullable types for optional params

nodes.label: Undocumented API Behavior
nodes.description: OpenAI docs say invalid strict schemas should be rejected, but API actually auto-normalizes and accepts them - creating unsatisfiable constraints silently

nodes.label: Bedrock Mantle (OpenAI Routing)
nodes.description: AWS Bedrock infrastructure that routes 'openai.*' models to /openai/v1/responses endpoint

nodes.label: Response Fields Ignored (24/30+)
nodes.description: Parser uses only 6 fields from 30+ in response (text, type, name, arguments, call_id, usage). Status, error, incomplete_details, moderation all ignored

edges.context: Without explicit strict:false, API auto-normalizes schemas to strict mode
Auto-normalization transforms optional params into required non-nullable fields, creating unsatisfiable constraints
Unsatisfiable constraints prevent GPT-5.5 from producing any valid output
GPT-5.5's literal compliance means it refuses rather than violates - older models would produce best-effort output
Empty output array triggers the bail!() crash in bedrock.rs response parser
bail!() generates 'Invalid Responses API response data' error shown to user
22 tools exceed soft limit of 20, increasing likelihood of constraint conflicts
Struct cannot represent additionalProperties:false, so ALL schemas violate strict mode
No validation in pipeline means non-compliant schemas pass through unchecked
Code was never reviewed, so inconsistency with openai.rs graceful handler was never caught
Unreviewed code didn't account for Responses API strict-mode auto-normalization difference
Responses API behavior: normalizes all schemas to strict when field omitted
Chat Completions defaults non-strict; Responses API defaults strict. Same schemas have different behavior
bedrock.rs:981-982 contains the crashing bail!() macro
openai.rs:427-437 contains the correct graceful handling pattern
bail!() should be replaced with warn!()+return empty pattern from openai.rs
function.rs:127-149 defines the JsonSchema struct that lacks additionalProperties
Most severe violator: 13/14 properties missing from required
Demonstrates impossible constraint: mutually exclusive params all become mandatory
Single compliant tool has no conflicts - confirms root cause is multi-tool constraint accumulation
Upstream rejected Responses API support, code added locally without review process
PR fixed empty output for Chat Completions only, identical issue in Responses API was missed
Adding strict:false opts out of auto-normalization, restoring best-effort behavior
Replacing bail!() with warn!()+return provides defense-in-depth for all empty output scenarios
Making schemas fully strict-compliant would allow strict:true to work correctly
API should reject invalid strict schemas per docs but instead silently normalizes creating traps
Bedrock routes openai.* models to /openai/v1/responses endpoint
bedrock.rs builds requests that route through Bedrock Mantle to OpenAI Responses API
Parser ignores status/error/incomplete_details fields that could provide diagnostic info before crashing
With strict:false, API won't normalize schemas, model can use best-effort matching
Graceful handling means empty output returns warning instead of user-facing error
